description: View forcing propagation as a peeling wave on a Tanner-like graph whose variable nodes are witness vertices and whose check nodes are local certificate templates. Then use spatial coupling across recursive layers so a tiny boundary seed launches a long exact-certificate wave with lower cost density than uncoupled repetition.
mathematical_formalization: Let H=(V,C,E) with variable nodes V and local certificate checks C. Define T_{t+1}=T_t \cup \{v\in V\setminus T_t : \exists c\in C,\ \mathrm{supp}(c)\subseteq T_t\cup\{v\},\ c(v)=(a,-a)\}. Partition V=\bigsqcup_i V_i with coupling window w and search for geometries where activation of V_i forces activation of V_{i+1} while minimizing S=(m+r)/(n-t).
analogical_connections: Forcing pairs as peeling decoders on sparse graphs.
Recursive copies as spatially coupled code sections.
Exact certificate growth as a decoding avalanche.
implementation_hypothesis: Start from a small verified gadget, chain copies into d_1 x d_2 x d_3 ladders with sparse inter-slab edges, estimate wave viability by density-evolution style simulation, and exact-verify only geometries whose wave front survives.
experiment_seed: Use 6-10 coupled slabs built from one tiny verified gadget, sweep coupling width and boundary seeds, and compare exact score against uncoupled repeats at matched edge density.

novelty_claim: The novelty is importing spatial coupling specifically to engineer exact arithmetic-certificate propagation, not parity-check decoding or sparse recovery.
differentiation: The checks are signed arithmetic singleton certificates rather than parity constraints, and the objective is witness score density instead of communication threshold.
